BiblicalUsage: Anak was a Canaanite, the father of the Anakim — the giants the spies saw in the land, strong people in walled cities, and the name stands for the giants themselves and for the fear they put in Israel. A generation later Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak, Sheshai and Ahiman and Talmai, the children of Anak.
TheologicalSignificance: A name for a giant carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the fear — the spies saw the children of Anak and said the land could not be taken, and Caleb drove them out anyway.
RelatedPeople: Anak; Sheshai, Son of Anak; Ahiman, Son of Anak; Talmai, Son of Anak
